chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan and Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of them, peace be upon them, that he was asked about a slave: may he lead the people in prayer if they are pleased with him and he is the most versed among them in the Qur'an? He said:
There is no harm in it.

key_terms.أَيَؤُمُّ: may he lead; referring to acting as Imam for the congregation in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: a slave; the person whose eligibility to lead the prayer is being asked about
key_terms.الْقَوْمَ: the people; the congregation being led in prayer
key_terms.رَضُوا: they are pleased; indicating the congregation's acceptance of him
key_terms.قُرْآنًا: Qur'an; meaning greater proficiency in Qur'an recitation
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; a formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Can a slave lead the congregation in salat (prayer) if the people accept him and he is the most proficient in the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a slave may lead the people in salat (prayer) if they are content with him and he is the most proficient of them in Qur'an recitation. It reflects that suitability for leading prayer is tied to accepted qualifications rather than social status alone.
